extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants for the Damon Runyon Quantitative Biology Fellowship (postdoctoral/early-career scientists in quantitative biology)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required forms for preparing and submitting an application for the Damon Runyon Quantitative Biology Fellowship, including eligibility windows, required documents, mentor requirements, proposal content and formatting, and letter submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be submitted through Proposal Central by 4:00 PM Eastern Time on December 1, 2026. No hard copies or emailed applications will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application instructions and relevant forms will be available on Proposal Central. Ensure submission before the stated deadline and via the specified portal; alternate submission methods are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree conferral eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree conferred between: December 1, 2021 - December 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a copy of diploma to confirm date. Applicants who have completed all PhD requirements but not yet received diploma may submit a letter from their graduate school explicitly stating completion dates (see Diploma requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joined mentor's lab eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Joined Mentor's Lab on or after: December 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This date requirement defines allowable start date with Mentor for eligibility. Combined with the 'not been in their Mentors’ labs for more than 24 months' rule, verify lab-start timing against the application deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum prior time in Mentor's lab
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not have been in their Mentors’ labs for more than 24 months prior to the application deadline date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate total time in Mentor's lab up to the deadline; exceeding 24 months makes applicant ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and type of Mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: This fellowship requires two Mentors (one from a dry lab and wet lab setting) and both Mentors must fill out the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor pair should represent interdisciplinary training (dry + wet). Each Mentor must complete required mentor forms; teams lacking both types of mentors or missing mentor forms will be incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor biosketch format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Mentor’s Biosketch in NIH format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH biosketch format (samples provided). Provide complete, current biosketches for both Mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor Letter of Support contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Mentor’s Letter of Support evaluating the candidate’s qualifications for the proposed research project and an assessment of the candidate’s potential for successful independent cancer research in the quantitative biology space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should speak to candidate qualifications and potential for independent research specifically in quantitative biology; letters from Mentors are distinct from reference letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Mentor’s Mentorship Track Record with names and current positions of graduate and postdoctoral trainees from the past 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a list showing prior trainees and their current positions to document mentor experience in training researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A single Training Plan for the candidate from the Mentors, up to two pages. The training plan for the candidate must be written jointly elaborating specifically on the interdisciplinary nature of the fellowship and feasibility/advantage of the dual mentorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must be jointly authored by both Mentors; describe concrete, feasible interdisciplinary training activities and advantages from dual mentorship. Preference will be given to mentorship teams where the labs are in close physical proximity to encourage frequent in person training; labs may be at same or distinct institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for physical proximity of labs
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference will be given to mentorship teams where the labs are in close physical proximity to encourage frequent in person training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how proximity will enable frequent in-person mentorship; if labs are at different institutions, explain arrangements to ensure effective training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters: quantity and source
rubrics_metrics.description: Three letters of reference are required from qualified individuals, other than the candidate's Mentors, who can evaluate the candidate's qualifications for the proposed research project and assess the candidate's potential for successful independent cancer research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For candidates with a PhD, one of the reference letters must come from the candidate's thesis advisor. Reference letters must be from individuals other than the Mentors and must evaluate qualifications and potential for independent cancer research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters: submission timing and application lock
rubrics_metrics.description: All reference letters must be submitted on or before the application deadline. Applicants will NOT be able to submit their application unless all reference letters are uploaded to the portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with referees to ensure letters are uploaded before the deadline; incomplete letter uploads block application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant NIH Biosketch format
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s Biosketch in NIH format (non-fellowship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH non-fellowship biosketch sample provided. Do not complete the 'Scholastic Performance' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant bibliography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's Bibliography, a separate list with hyperlinks to each publication (in addition to the NIH Biosketch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a separate, hyperlinked list of publications beyond what appears in the NIH biosketch. Ensure links are live and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Letter (~two pages) required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's Letter, approximately two pages including: description of previous research and teaching experience; statement on the transformative impact they had on their field of research as a graduate student; statement of interest in quantitative biology; if applicant is training at the same institution in which received their degree, an explanation of the reason(s) for remaining at the same institution (can be copied from page 2 of cover sheet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the letter to ~2 pages and address each listed element; be specific about prior contributions and motivations for quantitative biology. If staying at same institution, provide a clear rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Personal Statement (one page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's Personal Statement, a one-page narrative including: What they anticipate gaining from this award with respect to its impact and their career development. Optional: personal background (Applicants may choose to describe experiences that have influenced their current educational and career goals. Applicants may discuss challenges that they have faced while pursuing careers in research.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit to one page. Discuss concrete gains from the award and optional personal background material if relevant; optional elements may highlight diversity/overcoming challenges but are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Applicant's Long-Term Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of Applicant's Long-Term Commitment to a career in cancer research. This statement should be no longer than one paragraph and indicate what applicant plans to do after completing their postdoc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep to one paragraph; concisely describe career trajectory and commitment to cancer research post-training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal page limit and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Proposal including figures and/or tables incorporated into the text, not to exceed five pages of single-spaced, 12-point type with at least 0.5-inch margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and tables must be inside the five pages. Use required font size and margins; proposals exceeding the page limit or improper formatting risk non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal required content
rubrics_metrics.description: In the proposal, the applicant should: provide a summary of the research proposed (this is in addition to the required summary form); provide a brief background to the proposed research; state specific research objectives/aims; describe concisely the method of approach for the proposed research; explain the significance of the proposed research to the Foundation’s goals: understanding the causes and mechanisms of cancer and developing more effective cancer therapies and prevention; demonstrate the relevance of own background and the background and previous work of the Mentors and any other investigators to the proposed research; list references including the full title of each work cited—references are not included in the five page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address each listed element clearly and concisely within the five-page limit. References (with full titles) are required and do not count toward the five pages. Tie the proposed work explicitly to Damon Runyon’s goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational innovation paragraph (<=250 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief paragraph, no more than 250 words, concisely describing the innovation of the computational methods for the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize what is novel about the computational methods and why they represent an innovation; keep to 250 words or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational challenges paragraph (<=250 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief paragraph, no more than 250 words, concisely describing the computational challenges that currently prevent the field from answering the question that you propose to solve in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and concisely describe the key computational barriers; limit to 250 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of computational tools to develop/modify
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the computational tools you plan to develop and/or modify to use in your proposal that will overcome these challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify planned software/methodological developments or adaptations and how they will address stated challenges; be concrete about deliverables and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Research Form (abstract) length
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of Research Form, not to exceed one page (same as Abstracts tab, copy/paste).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a one-page summary/abstract that matches the Summary of Research form and is suitable for reviewers; copy/paste content between tabs as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration letters (optional, up to two)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration Letters. If applicable, up to two letters from collaborators indicating their willingness to contribute equipment, materials, or expertise (not reference letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit to two letters; they should document concrete collaborator commitments (equipment, materials, expertise). Do not substitute these for the required reference letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant diploma or graduate school letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy of the Applicant's Diploma. Applicants who have not yet received their PhD diploma but have successfully completed all PhD requirements, including PhD defense, may submit a letter from their graduate school explicitly stating such, with the dates of the PhD defense and degree conferral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a copy of the diploma if available. If diploma is pending, include an official graduate school letter stating completion and dates; this serves as proof of degree conferral for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: References formatting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: List references including the full title of each work cited—references are not included in the five page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete reference entries including full titles; placement outside the five-page proposal text so they do not count toward the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Research Support Form (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's Research Support Form (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of current/ongoing support if relevant; follow form instructions on Proposal Central.
